study type: Retrospective cross-sectional study using national registry data
exposure: childbirth intervention rates (induction of labour, augmentation of labour, pain medication, instrumental birth, caesarean section, paediatric involvement)
outcome: adverse maternal outcomes (including severe postpartum haemorrhage)
cohort: The study included all single childbirths from 37 weeks' gestation onwards in the Netherlands between 2010 and 2013.
finding: Most regional variation in childbirth interventions was found for type of pain medication and paediatric involvement, and notably, adverse neonatal and maternal outcomes were not lower in regions with higher intervention rates.
mod_finding: Rates for instrumental vaginal births varied between 16-19% (nulliparous) and 3-4% (multiparous), and intrapartum caesarean sections varied between 13-15% and 5-6% respectively, showing less regional variation compared to other interventions.
